text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/streaming/generate (eu-west-2). Current p99 2.7s (baseline 0.9s). Error rate unchanged. Affected model: open-llm-int8-v2 (recent precision profile rollout). Auto-fallback attempts: 3. Paging oncall.

Alex (oncall): seeing the alert, joining. any initial console links?

IncidentBot: Grafana -> https://graf.example.com/d/streaming/stream-latency?panelId=7&orgId=1 , traces: https://trace.example.com/trace/0a1b2c

Iris (sre): I can repro the tail spike in traces — lots of streaming stalls at token ~640 with long KV lookups. Looks correlated with int8 calibration 2026-03-15T02:00 rollout to eu-west-2 pool.

Mike (infra): confirming, the deployment used new quant profile int8-aggressive-2026-03. Autoscaler didn't trigger extra nodes; we had sustained slot saturation on 4 nodes. batching config also bumped max_batch_tokens -> 512 yesterday.

Juno (eng-ml): int8-aggressive-2026-03 included a dequant path optimization that changes KV layout; it's faster on average but can degrade worst-case when sequence length and cache misses align. We saw similar in perf tests but not at scale.

Alex (oncall): quick triage checklist: 1) mitigate customer impact 2) collect evidence for rollback or patch 3) hand off if needed. Iris — can you start mitigation? I'll loop CS.

Iris (sre): mitigation plan: a) route streaming traffic for affected model in eu-west-2 to fallback pool running fp16 variant b) temporarily lower max_batch_tokens to 256 for streaming routes c) enable prefix KV caching for popular prefixes. Executing now.

Iris (sre): running routing change: `rbacctl route update --service streaming --model open-llm-int8-v2 --region eu-west-2 --target fallback-fp16-pool --pct 100 --reason "p99 spike"`

IncidentBot: routing change initiated by Iris at 5032110005. Watch latency.

Alex (oncall): Sara, can you draft a quick customer-facing note for any users on dedicated/dedicated+private who might be impacted? Prioritize accounts with high SLA.

Sara (cs): on it. Short note: "We observed elevated tail latency impacting streaming generation for customers in EU-West. We’ve routed requests to a fallback model and are monitoring. No data loss; minimal feature impact. Expect updates in 30m." Sending to major customers and ops@.

Mike (infra): reduced batching: `kubectl patch config batching-config -n inference -p '{"spec":{"maxBatchTokens":256}}'` patch applied at 5032110032. Confirming rollout to 6/6 nodes.

Juno (eng-ml): toggled KV prefix caching for top prefixes in eu-west-2 via experiment flags. Hoping this avoids cold-KV stalls.

Iris (sre): early signal: p99 dropped from 2.7s -> 1.1s within 90s of routing change and batch cap; p95 stable. Streaming stalls still present at very long contexts >1200 tokens but far less frequent.

Alex (oncall): good. next: decide whether to roll back int8-aggressive-2026-03 in eu-west-2 or to roll forward with a calibration patch. Juno, how quick is a calibration fallback (less aggressive quant offsets)?

Juno (eng-ml): can cut a soft rollback profile (int8-stable-2026-02) and push to the pool in ~15-20 minutes. Alternatively, a hotfix to KV access path could be riskier and take longer.

Iris (sre): ops preference: soft rollback to previous profile for now — lower risk and restores tail behavior. Keep fp16 fallback enabled until we verify.

Alex (oncall): agreed. Mike, do we have capacity to deploy the previous profile and safely restart workers without customers noticing? We should avoid full drain if possible.

Mike (infra): yes. We'll hot-swap the profile in the model config and do a rolling restart with minimal disruption: `fleetctl update-profile --model open-llm-int8-v2 --profile int8-stable-2026-02 --region eu-west-2` I'll run at 5032110120.

PagerDuty-Bot: Notification: Alex acknowledged the page. Next oncall: Iris in 1h.

Alex (oncall): running the profile swap now.

Mike (infra): profile swap started at 5032110120. Rolling restart strategy: 1 pod at a time, health-checks 30s, concurrency 1.

Iris (sre): monitoring logs: some pods reported increased startup time due to model load; two pods transiently failed health probe and were cycled — all back healthy now.

IncidentBot: metric update: p99 at 5032110180 -> 0.95s, p95 0.28s. Streaming stalls largely gone in sampled traces.

Sara (cs): sent customer note to top 12 accounts and posted short update to status.redwood.ai. A few customers replied asking for root cause ETA.

Alex (oncall): let's capture RCA artifacts: traces, kube events, quant profile diffs, and perf test logs. Juno, please open a ticket in #eng-ml with checklist for a follow-up: deeper analysis and test harness to reproduce at scale.

Juno (eng-ml): creating ticket INF-2026-334: "int8-aggressive-2026-03 tail latency regression — reproduce & mitigate". Will attach traces and perf runs. Owners: Juno, Mike. ETA 48h.

Iris (sre): post-mortem notes inline: probable root cause = dequant KV layout optimization causing cache-unfriendly access pattern for long contexts, exposing worst-case KV lookup time; exacerbated by increased max_batch_tokens. Mitigations = rollback to stable profile, cap batch tokens, route to fallback, adjust caching, add canary + perf test that simulates long-context streaming.

Alex (oncall): handing off to Iris for monitoring and post-incident follow-up. I'll update the incident board and mark this as "mitigation in place". If anything regresses, re-page.

Iris (sre): taking over. I'll run 1h watch and schedule a 0900 postmortem sync with eng-ml + infra + cs. Thanks everyone.

Mike (infra): added a temporary alert: if p99 > 1.5s for 5m in eu-west-2 on streaming, auto-route to fallback and notify oncall. Config: `alertmanager/alerts.yml` updated.

Juno (eng-ml): quick note: we'll add a targeted perf test to the CI that runs long-context streaming (seq len 1600) under int8-aggressive profile to catch this going forward.

Sara (cs): customers acknowledged; a couple asked for timeline on a permanent fix. I put them on the follow-up invite.

Alex (oncall): closing thread for now — status: mitigated, rollback applied, monitoring. Last checked at 5032110250. If we get noisy alerts, reopen.

IncidentBot: Incident closed for now (mitigated). Reference: INC-50321-quant-flare-2026."
